title: The Peninsular Peninsular Plateaus
definition: The Peninsular Plateau is a tableland composed of the older crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks, formed due to the breaking and drifting of the Gondwana land, making it the oldest and most stable landmass of India.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Geography GS-1 (Physiography, drainage systems, mineral resource distribution, and geological history). Frequently tested in Prelims via location of plateaus, hill ranges, and river flow directions.
learningOutcomes: Master the geological evolution and tectonic history of the Peninsular Plateau.
Evaluate spatial distribution, regional sub-divisions, and mineral wealth of different plateaus.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions regarding hill ranges and plateaus.
